name: Chhulung
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Limbu, Man Kumari. An ethnolinguistic observation of Chhulung Rai, a highly endangered language (thesis).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1/5.3 languoid chhu1238; OLAC page for cur (Wayback 2026-06-07); Ethnologue 'Chhiling' cur (Wayback 2024-11-30); Wikipedia 'Chulung language'.
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog lists only the three Limbu items (plus Gerber 2023 pp. 68-69 on subclassification and Campbell et al. 2022 on endangerment); OLAC lists no descriptive resource beyond Glottolog/Ethnologue/LINGUIST List; Ethnologue names Chhiling with no dialects; Wikipedia has no phonology section. Nepalese Linguistics vols 25 and 29 also grepped: no Chhulung matter; vols 24 and 30 arrived truncated from Wayback.

sources.citation: Rai, Ichchha Purna. 2017. The Kirati ritual language: evidence from Chhintang and Chhulung. Gipan 3(2): 104-113. doi:10.3126/gipan.v3i2.48915.
sources.note: Nothing; ritual-register binomials (notes only that the two limbs of a binomial share their final syllable).

sources.citation: Rai, Ichchha Purna. 2013. A contrastive study of Chhintang and English pronouns: problems and teaching strategies. Nepalese Linguistics 28: 155-161. (Same volume: Paudyal, Netra P. 2013. Issues of v-v compounds in Chintang, pp. 125ff.)
sources.note: Nothing on Chhulung stress. Rai's paper is on Chhintang (uses 'Chhulung' once, p. 159) and its 'no voice and no tone' line is Ethnologue's Chintang note; Paudyal p. 125 names 'Chɨlɨng (also pronounced as Chiling or Chulung)' with Athpare and Belhare as Chintang's nearest relatives.

sources.citation: Rai, Ichchha Purna. 2013. English tense and aspect: EFL problems that Chhulung learners have. Journal of NELTA 17(1-2). doi:10.3126/nelta.v17i1-2.8093.
Limbu, Man Kumari. 2012. Tense and aspect in Chhulung. Nepalese Linguistics 27: 85-88.
sources.note: Nothing; tense/aspect morphology. p. 85 gives the ethnonym's phonetic form: 'The term Chhulung is pronounced with unrounded central vowel [ɨ] and its true phonetic transcription is [tsʰɨlɨŋ]'. Not in Glottolog's list.

sources.citation: Limbu, Man Kumari. 2007 [approval letter dated 2064/11/07 BS]. An ethnolinguistic observation of Chhulung Rai, a highly endangered language. Final narrative report to the Social Inclusion Research Fund (SIRF/SNV Nepal), apprenticeship grant SIRF/AG/07, supervised by Madhav P. Pokharel (TU). 50 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2 'Phonology' (pp. 15-26) gives 26 consonant and 6 vowel phonemes with minimal pairs, Devanagari orthography and pronouns; the conclusion list (p. 25) notes 'Vowels length is not phonemic', 'not any diphthongs so far', 'not any dialect so far'. The words stress/accent/tone/pitch/syllable never occur. Original host (socialinclusion.org.np) is dead; fetched sources from the Wayback snapshot of 2016-04-10.
